### Step 25d — Twelve smaller real bugs found by the same QC review, bundled per this project's established pattern
Each confirmed by direct code read (not all independently reproduced, per the review's own confidence-labeling — see each item), same "found while auditing, not caused by any specific recent step" framing as Step 9e/9f.

1. **Library's bulk-series translate ignores the monthly spending cap**, and hardcodes the `audio_drama` style guide even for narration/novel dramas, uses each engine's bare default model rather than the drama's chosen one, and never sets `gpu_touching=True` for an Ollama engine (risking it running outside Step 5c's GPU-job guard). Workspace and the CLI both correctly enforce the monthly cap; this is the one path that doesn't. A dead `character_names` variable in the same function is also worth deleting while this is fixed.
2. **A job queued behind the GPU guard is invisible in the UI.** The transcribe/translate(Ollama)/flag/consistency/emotion/fix-flagged/notes job panels only render running/done/error states — nothing for queued. The one `st.info` that would announce "queued" is discarded by an immediately-following `st.rerun()`. Clicking the button again while queued just says "already running," and there's no way to cancel a queued job from these panels (`background_jobs.cancel_queued` exists and works, but only `live_tab.py` actually calls it).
3. **The "fix flagged lines in bulk" job can lose already-completed paid work on any exception.** Its re-transcription call sits inside a bare `try/finally`, so a real exception (e.g. a model-download failure partway through) escapes without being caught, and `db.save_lines` only runs once at the very end — so every line fixed before the exception is lost, not just the one that failed. A separate `except Exception: pass` around the translation half of the same job silently swallows auth/quota errors, leaving the user with just "Fixed 0 of N" and no explanation why.
4. **Auto-tune crashes if the page is refreshed while a run is in progress.** The "job just finished" branch appends to `_autotune["results"]` with no None-check; the "still running" branch already has one — a straightforward missing guard in the newer of the two branches.
5. **The glossary "enforce exact match" substitution pass can silently overwrite a user's own live edit mid-translation-job.** It rewrites `en` on every one of the job's own (now-stale) in-memory line copies after the fact — if a user edits a line's English while the job is still running and a glossary term happens to match, the substitution pass's write wins even though its baseline text is now stale, clobbering the user's edit with no warning.
6. **Some export paths don't clamp overlapping subtitle cues**, despite Workspace's own export promising "never export an overlapping (invalid) cue": `export_package.py`, Library's "Export all," and `cli.py export-video` all skip the existing `subtitle_formats.clamp_overlaps` call that Workspace's own export path already uses.
7. **A few call sites still build a translation engine without the drama's Ollama URL or Gemini free-tier flag** — the same bug shape Step 5b item 1 already fixed once elsewhere, recurring in three places that weren't covered by that fix: romanization credits (`workspace_tab.py` ~line 1294), Diagnostics' own accuracy-benchmark runner, and Navigator.
8. **"🗑️ Delete this drama" in Workspace has no confirmation step at all** — it deletes every database row for the drama and `rmtree`s its folder immediately on click, with no check for a still-running job on that drama. Library's own bulk-delete already requires a "Confirm delete" checkbox; this is the one delete path in the app that doesn't match this project's own standing "destructive actions need a separate, explicit confirmation defaulting to No" rule.
9. **Diagnostics' own "expected top-level files" / "expected tabs files" lists are stale**, missing 14 real modules including hard imports like `portable.py`, `applog.py`, `subtitle_formats.py`, `resegment.py`, `raw_transcript.py`, `bulk_translate.py`, `audio_preprocess.py`, and `tabs/live_tab.py` — so the missing-file health check this list exists to power can no longer actually catch a genuinely missing file among these.
10. **Two CLI gaps**: `cli.py dub` has no `--tts-engine` flag at all, so it can only ever use edge-tts from the command line regardless of what's configured for the drama's characters; `cli.py align` ignores the drama's own saved alignment method, ASR backend, Whisper size, and glossary priming, rather than reading them the way the Workspace path does.
11. **`db.save_translation_notes` can accumulate orphaned duplicate notes.** It inserts a note with `line_id = NULL` when the target line no longer exists (`save_emotions` already correctly skips this case) — and since SQLite treats every `NULL` as distinct for uniqueness purposes, the app's own "one note per line and term" invariant doesn't catch these, so they can pile up indefinitely with nothing to clean them out.
12. **Scanlate's per-page translation context can leak between pages.** The "previous page" context key (`sc_context_<drama>`) holds whichever page was processed *most recently*, not the page actually before the one being processed — so re-detecting an earlier page after a later one has already run picks up the later page's context instead. `detect_notes_<page label>` has a related scoping gap: it isn't keyed by drama at all.
13. **Bulk-mode translation can also mark a drama "translated" with lines still missing** — found by Step 25c's implementing session while fixing the same root cause (item 4's shape) in the CLI/Workspace paths. `bulk_translate.py` (~lines 683, 976, 1315) doesn't share the guard Step 25c added there. Fix by wiring bulk mode into the same shared post-translate helper once it exists.
14. **Downloaded Piper voices aren't visible in Diagnostics' disk-management panel** — found by the same session while building Step 25c item 1's offline-voice picker. Step 9b's panel only scans the Hugging Face model cache; Piper voices download to `library/piper_voices` instead, so they're invisible to it and to whatever cleanup/disk-usage view relies on it.

### Step 25f — Fix: Navigator's main button always crashes, and baihehub search can never return a result — two real, confirmed bugs found in a Discover/unused-code audit (2026-09-26)
Found by a read-only audit of `tabs/discover_tab.py`, `tabs/navigator_tab.py` and the modules they call, at the user's request. Both reproduced directly, not inferred.

1. **Navigator's "🧭 Translate page + get navigation steps" raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'navigator'` every time.** `tabs/navigator_tab.py:59` does `import navigator`, but root-level `navigator.py` (the backend: `fetch_visible_labels`, `translate_labels`, `generate_navigation_steps`) was deleted in commit `4d25c9c` ("Declutter Workspace tab", 2026-09-22) alongside `discover.py`/`library.py`/`settings.py`/`workspace.py` — those four really were stale pre-`tabs/` copies, but `navigator.py` was not; it was the only implementation. The import sits outside the `try`, so `_safe_render` shows "The Navigator tab hit an error." No test imports it, which is why nothing caught this. **Fix:** restore it from history (`git show 4d25c9c^:navigator.py`), re-verify it against today's `translate_engines`/`page_fetch` APIs, add every `requests` call to the `timeout=` static check, and add a mocked test that the button's code path imports and runs. Confirmed by running the expression. On top of that the three endpoints are unverified guesses ("plausible API endpoint shapes"), and the query isn't URL-encoded. The UI's own warning tells users to install Playwright "so the app can render the page properly," but this function never uses Playwright — misleading advice. **Fix:** correct the precedence and URL-encode the query; then either verify a real endpoint (or route through `page_fetch.smart_fetch` so the Playwright advice becomes true), or, if no real endpoint exists, remove the automatic search and keep only the browser-fallback link, with the warning text changed to match.

**Exit:** Navigator's button runs end to end under a mocked engine/fetch (new test). A unit test feeds `search_baihehub` a mocked dict response and a mocked list response and gets results (or the function is removed and the UI shows only the fallback link). Manual check: click the Navigator button on a real page with a real key and see translated labels + steps.

### Step 25i — Fix: switching dramas can silently overwrite the new drama's EPUB with a leftover upload from the old one
Found by the planning session (2026-09-27) auditing `tabs/workspace_tab.py` for the same widget-key root cause as Step 25b, specifically checking whether the fix there (scoping section 6's keys by `picked_id`) was needed anywhere else in the file. It was — this is a real, unfixed instance of the same class of bug, not a hypothetical. **Not independently reproduced end-to-end in a running app by this session (no browser available here) — confirmed by direct code read, the same initial-confidence level Steps 25/25b/25c started from before their own fixes were built and tested.**

**The bug.** `epub_file = st.file_uploader("Upload .epub", type=["epub"], key="epub_upload")` (`tabs/workspace_tab.py:1979`) uses a **static key, not scoped by drama id** — unlike the widgets Step 25b fixed. Streamlit's file uploader keeps returning the same uploaded file object on every rerun until the user explicitly clears it or uploads a new one, regardless of what else changes on the page. The code immediately below has **no button gate on the write itself** — only chapter extraction is behind a button:
```
if epub_file:
    epub_path = os.path.join(ddir, "source.epub")
    with open(epub_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(epub_file.getbuffer())
```
`ddir` is always the *currently selected* drama's folder. So: upload an EPUB while on drama A, then switch to drama B without touching the uploader — on the very next render, drama B's `source.epub` is silently overwritten with drama A's file. No click, no confirmation, no warning. This is the same root cause as Step 25b (an unscoped widget key leaking one drama's data into another across a switch) but arguably more severe: 25b needed a save-triggering edit, this needs nothing but switching dramas while a file is still "selected" in the uploader.

**A smaller, related finding folded in here:** `force_retranslate = b2.checkbox(..., key="force_retranslate")` (`tabs/workspace_tab.py:2991`) is also a static, unscoped key. Checking it on drama A and then switching to drama B leaves it checked — clicking Translate on B then force-retranslates every already-translated line with no explicit re-confirmation on the new drama, a destructive default silently carrying over. Same root cause, lower severity (needs an explicit Translate click, doesn't overwrite a file on its own) — this project's own "destructive actions need a separate, explicit confirmation, defaulting to No" rule already covers the shape of what's missing here.

Also checked and found clean while auditing this: `gl_file_up` (glossary file uploader, same static-key pattern) is gated behind an explicit "📥 Import glossary file" button click, so it needs an affirmative action on the wrong drama to misfire, not just a switch — lower urgency, not included as its own item, but worth a second look if this step's fix pattern generalizes easily.

1. **Scope `epub_upload`'s key by `picked_id`**, the same fix direction Step 25b used (`key=f"epub_upload_{picked_id}"`), so switching dramas naturally resets the widget instead of carrying the old file forward.
2. **Also gate the raw file write behind an explicit action**, not just a truthy check on every render — defense in depth beyond the key fix alone, since a key-scoping fix alone still means the write happens on the very first accidental render with a real file selected. Match the existing "Import chapters from EPUB" button's gating.
3. **Scope `force_retranslate`'s key by `picked_id`** the same way.
4. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm this reproduces in a real running app (a real browser, not just code reading) before considering it closed — this session's own initial-confidence level here matches how Steps 25/25b/25c started, and both of those were confirmed by direct reproduction before their fix was accepted.

**Exit:**
- A test reproduces the exact bug: upload an EPUB while drama A is selected, switch to drama B without touching the uploader, and confirm drama B's `source.epub` is NOT overwritten with drama A's file.
- A test confirms checking `force_retranslate` on drama A and switching to drama B does not leave it checked for drama B.
- Manual check: upload an EPUB on one drama, switch to a different drama with the file still shown as selected, and confirm nothing gets written to the new drama's folder until an explicit action is taken.

**Built and pushed (`claude/step-25i-roadmap-fnaasq`), reviewed and approved by the planning session — real, well-built, exactly the fix this step's own text specified.** Independently verified: fetched fresh, confirmed genuinely current (merge-base equals the exact `baihe-subtitler` tip, PR #92's merge). The diff is minimal and precise (2 files, +133/-4): `epub_upload`'s key is scoped by `picked_id`, the write moved behind a new explicit "💾 Save this EPUB to this drama" button, and `force_retranslate`'s key is scoped by `picked_id` too — the chapter picker now correctly reads from disk (`os.path.exists(epub_path)`) rather than being tied to the transient upload object, a small genuine improvement (a drama's already-saved EPUB now shows its chapter picker on return, not just right after upload) not a side effect. All three new tests independently re-run and confirmed to genuinely fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fix (not vacuous) — checked directly via `git checkout` of the old file, not taken on the report's word. ### Step 25k — Fix: "Restore from backup" destroys the entire library before it even checks whether the uploaded zip is valid
Found by the same QC review, **independently re-verified by direct code read before writing this step**.

**The bug.** Library's "♻️ Restore from backup" (`tabs/library_tab.py`, the block starting around line 516) does, in order: `shutil.rmtree(library_dir)` if it exists, `os.makedirs(library_dir, exist_ok=True)`, and only *then* `zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(restore_file.read()))` followed by `zf.extractall(library_dir)`. If the uploaded file isn't a valid zip, or is a valid zip that doesn't actually contain a library backup (the wrong file entirely — nothing checks for `library.db` inside it), `zipfile.ZipFile(...)` raises, the `except Exception as e: st.error(...)` block catches it and shows an error — but the library directory has already been deleted and recreated empty by then. The only safeguard before any of this runs is a generic "I understand this replaces all current library data" checkbox, which says nothing about what happens if the file itself is bad.

**Trigger:** click "Restore from backup" with any file that isn't a genuine library backup zip (a corrupted download, the wrong zip entirely, an empty file) and the confirmation checkbox ticked. The error message appears, but the entire library — every drama, every line, every character and glossary entry — is already gone, with no automatic backup taken first.

1. **Validate before destroying, not after.** Open and inspect the uploaded zip (`zipfile.ZipFile`, then confirm it contains a `library.db` member — the minimum real signal this is an actual backup, not just any zip) *before* touching the existing `library_dir` at all. Show a clear error and stop if it's invalid, with nothing yet deleted.
2. **Consider restoring to a staging directory and swapping it in**, rather than deleting in place — `zf.extractall()` into a fresh temp directory, confirm it extracted cleanly, then replace `library_dir` in one move/rename step. This also protects against a valid-zip-but-incomplete-extraction failure partway through, which the current code has no recovery from either.
3. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm the exact current code path (this may have shifted slightly since the QC review read it) before changing the order of operations.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms that restoring from an invalid zip (not a real zip file, or a zip missing `library.db`) leaves the existing library directory completely intact — nothing deleted, a clear error shown.
- A test confirms that restoring from a genuine, valid backup zip still works exactly as before.
- Manual check: with a real library containing at least one drama, attempt "Restore from backup" with an obviously-wrong file (e.g. a random zip or a corrupted download) and confirm the existing library is still there afterward, not wiped.

**Built and pushed (`claude/step-25k-roadmap-1yj5vo`), reviewed and approved by the planning session — real, well-built, and genuinely stronger than the minimal fix this step asked for.** Independently verified: fetched fresh, confirmed genuinely current. The diff (2 files, +125/-7) adds a new `restore_library_backup()` that validates the zip (opens it, confirms `library.db` is present, runs `zf.testzip()` for corruption) entirely before touching `library_dir`, extracts to a staging directory on the *same* filesystem (so the final swap is a real atomic `os.rename`, not a slow/riskier cross-device copy), and rolls back to the original directory if the final rename fails — item 2's own "consider a staging directory" suggestion, done well, not just item 1's minimum validate-first bar. ### Step 25l — Fix: undoing a merge can attach notes, emotions, and flags to the wrong line
Found by the same 2026-09-27 QC review; **independently re-verified by direct code read**, including a scratch-script reproduction of the exact failure the review described.

**The bug.** `core.adopt_ids` (`core.py:67-92`) matches each line in a restored snapshot back to a current line by id, falling back to matching by position (`idx`) only when the id lookup fails. That positional fallback exists for a real, legitimate case: snapshots saved before Step 2 (permanent line ids) recorded no id at all. But the same fallback also silently fires for a second, unintended case: **a snapshot line whose id genuinely existed at snapshot time but was deleted by an intervening merge.** `by_id.get(ln.id)` returns `None` for a merged-away id exactly the same way it would for a never-assigned one — `adopt_ids` can't tell the difference — so it falls back to matching by `idx`, and after a merge deletes a row, `idx` numbering shifts, so the fallback attaches the snapshot's notes/emotions/flags to whatever line now happens to sit at that position, not the line they actually belonged to.

**Reproduced directly** (scratch script, not just read): merged line "b" into "a", then restored the "before merge" snapshot — the note originally on "c" moved to "b", and "d"'s idiom flag moved to "c". Confirmed real, silent, and no error surfaces anywhere.

1. **Distinguish "no id ever recorded" from "id recorded but no longer exists."** The pre-Step-2 case should still fall back to positional matching; a post-merge case should not — matching a merged-away id positionally is never correct, since the merge specifically changed the drama's line count and ordering. Concretely: track whether the snapshot format itself is id-aware (Step 2 or later) separately from whether a specific line's id resolved — only fall back positionally for snapshots from before id tracking existed.
2. For an id-aware snapshot whose id no longer resolves (the merged-away case), the restored line should get a fresh id (as already happens when `match is None or match.id in used` falls through entirely) rather than being silently reattached to an unrelated line via position.
3. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm `adopt_ids`'s exact current logic and every one of its call sites (history-snapshot restore, translation-version activate) still match this description before changing it.

**Exit:**
- A test reproduces the exact bug: merge two lines, take a snapshot restore of the pre-merge state, and confirm the merged-away line's notes/emotions/flags do NOT attach to whatever line now sits at its old position.
- A test confirms a genuinely old, id-less snapshot still restores correctly via positional matching (the legitimate case must keep working).
- Manual check: merge two lines with distinct notes on nearby lines, restore the pre-merge snapshot, and confirm every note ends up on the line it actually belongs to.

**Built and pushed (`step-25l-merge-undo-notes`), reviewed and approved by the planning session — real, well-built, exactly the fix this step's own text specified.** Independently verified: fetched fresh, confirmed genuinely current. The diff (2 files, +51/-4) tracks `id_was_recorded` separately from whether the id resolved, and only falls back to positional matching `if match is None and not id_was_recorded` — a merged-away id now correctly gets a fresh id instead of a stale positional misattachment, and the genuinely old id-less case still restores positionally as before. Ran the branch's own tests directly: `test_line_ids.py`, 19 passed, 0 failed. Approved — tell the implementing session to open the PR.

### Step 25n — Fix: a failed Scanlate page translation silently blanks every bubble instead of showing an error
Found by the same QC review; **independently re-verified by direct code read**, confirmed exact mechanism.

**The bug.** `translate_page_with_context` (`scanlate.py`, the block ending around line 928) returns `[""] * len(texts)` — a same-length list of empty strings — whenever the LLM's JSON response fails to parse or is missing a `"translations"` key (a truncated response from `max_tokens=1500` on a text-heavy page is a real, plausible trigger). Because the returned list is the *same length* as what was sent, `translate_page_bubbles` (`scanlate.py:1747-1775`) — whose own length check exists specifically to catch a mismatched result and refuse it — doesn't catch this case at all: the lengths match, so it proceeds to `b["translated_text"] = t or ""` for every eligible bubble, overwriting whatever was there before, including a hand-edited translation. No exception is raised anywhere in this path, so the caller shows normal success, not the "nothing was changed" warning a real failure should produce. Batch mode shares the same function, so the same failure mode applies there too.

1. **Make a parse failure distinguishable from a genuine empty-translations result**, e.g. by returning `None` (or raising) rather than a same-length list of blanks, and have `translate_page_bubbles` treat that as a refusal — same "don't apply a result there's no safe way to trust" principle the length-mismatch check already applies, just extended to cover this case too.
2. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm the exact current shape of both functions (this may have shifted since the review) before changing the failure-signaling contract between them.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms a malformed/unparseable LLM response does NOT overwrite existing bubble translations — either an exception is raised or the bubbles are left untouched, with a clear error shown.
- A test confirms a genuinely empty `"translations": []` response (the LLM legitimately found nothing to translate) is still handled correctly, distinct from a parse failure.
- Manual check: hand-edit a bubble's translation, then trigger a page translation in a way that forces a malformed response (a very low `max_tokens` on a text-heavy page is one way), and confirm the hand-edit survives rather than being silently blanked.

**Built and pushed (`claude/step-25n-roadmap-wonrvh`), reviewed and approved by the planning session — real, well-built, exactly the fix this step's own text specified.** Independently verified: fetched fresh, confirmed genuinely current. The diff (2 files, +67/-6) makes `translate_page_with_context` return `None` on a genuine parse failure (no response, unparseable JSON, missing `"translations"` key), distinct from a real empty-translations result which still passes through unchanged, and `translate_page_bubbles` raises a clear `ValueError` before the length check when it sees `None` rather than applying a same-length blank list. Ran the branch's own tests directly: `test_scanlate_regions.py`, 38 passed, 0 failed. Full combined trial-merge suite (with 25m/25r/25s together): 2490 passed, 46 skipped, 0 failed. Approved.

### Step 25o — Fix: Find & replace (Workspace and Scanlate) can misapply a stale match after the underlying lines/bubbles change
Found by the same QC review; **independently re-verified by direct code read** for the Workspace case; the Scanlate case's DB-write mechanism confirmed directly, the follow-on widget-staleness claim taken at the review's own stated confidence (not independently traced end to end).

**The bug, Workspace (`tabs/workspace_tab.py:3927-3955`).** "Preview matches" computes and stores `{"idx": ..., "new_text": ...}` pairs in session state at preview time. "Apply" re-maps those pairs onto whatever line currently sits at each `idx` — with no check that the line at that position is still the same one that was actually matched. If a merge or re-segmentation runs between Preview and Apply, `idx` numbering shifts, and the replacement lands on an unrelated line. If the originally-matched line's own text is hand-edited and saved in between, Apply's stale `new_text` silently overwrites that edit. Apply also never clears the `en_<idx>` widget state after writing to the database, so the on-screen text can keep showing the pre-replacement value until an unrelated refresh, and a subsequent "Save edits" from that stale display would undo the replacement.

**The related bug, Scanlate (`tabs/scanlate_tab.py:525-538`).** Bulk find-and-replace's "Apply" correctly writes by bubble id via `db.update_bubble_text` (not positional — this part is sound), but doesn't touch the on-screen bubble text-area widgets (`btr_<id>`), which keep showing the pre-replacement text. The success message tells the user to "re-render affected pages" — which only affects the rendered image output, not these edit widgets — so a subsequent "Save bubble edits" from the still-stale widgets would revert the just-applied replacement. `sc_fr_matches` (the Scanlate preview-match session-state key) is also not scoped by drama, a smaller related issue worth fixing in the same pass.

1. **Workspace**: re-validate each match's line still has the expected old text (or re-key matches by line `id`, checked against a fresh reload) at Apply time, not just at Preview time — refuse or re-preview if anything's changed underneath. Clear the affected `en_<idx>` widget state after Apply, the same way other line-mutating actions in this file already do.
2. **Scanlate**: clear or refresh the affected bubble's text-area widget state after Apply, so the display matches what was just written to the database. Scope `sc_fr_matches` by drama id.
3. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm both call sites' exact current shape before changing them — this session traced the Workspace case fully but not the Scanlate widget-staleness claim end to end.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms Workspace's Apply refuses (or re-checks) when a matched line's text has changed since Preview, rather than overwriting it with the stale replacement.
- A test confirms Workspace's Apply clears the affected lines' widget state so a subsequent Save doesn't revert the replacement.
- A test confirms Scanlate's Apply either clears the affected bubbles' widget state or that a subsequent "Save bubble edits" doesn't revert an applied replacement.
- Manual check: preview a Workspace find-and-replace, merge two unrelated lines before clicking Apply, and confirm the replacement lands only on the originally-matched line's real content, not whatever now sits at its old position.

**Merged as PR #107** — opened and merged directly by this planning session after independent verification: read the full diff (Workspace re-keys by permanent line `id` instead of `idx`, re-checks each line's current text against the previewed `old_text` before applying and skips+warns on any that changed; Scanlate re-keys `sc_fr_matches` by drama id and clears each edited bubble's `btr_<id>` widget state before rerun), trial-merged cleanly against the tip at merge time, ran `tests/test_review_workspace.py` + `tests/test_scanlate_tab.py` directly (30/30 passed), CI green.

### Step 25q — Fix: two real gaps in ToS enforcement — a frozen verdict, and automated requests search/browse/tracked-series-checking never check at all
Found by the same QC review; **independently re-verified by direct code read**, both confirmed exactly.

**Gap 1 — a source's ToS verdict is frozen at its first import.** `sources/ladder.py`'s `load_capabilities` (`~282-286`) returns the source's **stored** capability record whenever one exists, and completely ignores the adapter's own built-in `default` record in that case — even though every import already saves a stored record (`record_ladder_result`, wired in by Step 25g). If an adapter's own built-in capabilities are later edited to mark a source `tos_prohibited=True` (the exact kind of update this project's own "re-verify" discipline calls for when a site's terms change), anyone who already has a stored record for that source from an earlier import will never see the update — `check_terms` keeps consulting the stale stored verdict, not the corrected built-in one.

**Gap 2 — the ToS check only guards Preview and Import, not search, browsing, or the periodic tracked-series checker.** Confirmed directly: `sources/registry.py`'s `multi_search` (`~111-133`) calls `adapter.search(query)` with no `check_terms` anywhere in the path; `sources/chapter_check.py`'s `check_series` (`~26-29`, the periodic background job that polls tracked series for new chapters) calls `adapter.get_chapters(...)` the same way. A source marked ToS-prohibited still gets automated search requests and periodic automated chapter-list polling — the two places `check_terms` was added (Step 25g) don't cover everywhere the app actually talks to a source.

1. **For Gap 1**: when a stored record and the adapter's own built-in default disagree specifically on `tos_prohibited`, prefer whichever one says prohibited (a stored `False` shouldn't be able to override a corrected built-in `True`) — or, more simply, re-derive the ToS fields from the adapter's built-in default on every load rather than persisting them at all, since ToS status is a property of the site, not of what was observed on a past request.
2. **For Gap 2**: call `check_terms` (or skip a prohibited adapter entirely, same effect) in `multi_search`'s per-adapter worker and in `chapter_check.check_series`, matching the guard already in place for Preview/Import.
3. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm both locations' exact current shape, and check whether any other call site talks to an adapter without going through `check_terms` — this may not be an exhaustive list.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms a source whose *built-in* default is ToS-prohibited is refused even when a stale stored record says otherwise.
- A test confirms `multi_search` skips (or refuses) a ToS-prohibited source rather than including it in search results.
- A test confirms the tracked-series checker skips a ToS-prohibited source rather than polling it for new chapters.
- Manual check: mark a source ToS-prohibited, confirm it's excluded from search results and from the tracked-series background check, not just from direct import.

**Built and pushed (`claude/step-25q-roadmap-hj7202`), reviewed and approved by the planning session — real, well-built, and covers a real call site beyond what this step's own text listed.** Independently verified: fetched fresh, confirmed genuinely current. 1. **Scanlate's "Add bubble" (manual add) does nothing — independently confirmed.** `tabs/scanlate_tab.py:305-309` appends the new bubble to a local `edited_bubbles` list inside the "Add bubble" button's own click branch, but the save call (`db.save_bubbles(page["id"], edited_bubbles)`, line ~407) only runs inside a *different* button's own click branch ("Save bubble edits"). Since only one button's click is "true" per script run, clicking Add doesn't also trigger Save in the same run — the appended bubble is discarded the moment the script ends. Also confirmed: the entire manual-add section only renders inside `if bubbles:` (a page where detection found nothing has no way to add one manually at all, despite Scanlate's own caption text suggesting exactly that as the recovery path). Fix: make the appended bubble actually persist (either auto-save on Add, or keep it in a durable per-page session-state list that the Save button includes), and move the manual-add UI outside the `if bubbles:` gate so a zero-detection page can still get one.
2. **"🗑️ Remove raw novel context" doesn't stick — independently confirmed.** `tabs/workspace_tab.py:1769-1787`: the uploader (`key=f"raw_novel_{picked_id}"`, correctly drama-scoped, unlike item 8's cousin above) still holds the previously-uploaded file after Remove's `st.rerun()`, and the unconditional `if raw_novel_file is not None: ... write` immediately above re-creates the just-deleted file from the still-selected upload. Fix: also clear the uploader's own widget state on Remove (not just delete the file), or gate the write behind an explicit Save the same way Step 25i/25p do elsewhere.
3. **CLI/Workspace translate produce different output for the same drama — at the review's own confidence, not independently traced line-by-line by this session.** `cli.py translate` (`~270-280`) builds glossary terms and style guidelines but, per the review, leaves out emotion guidance, the learned style profile, the she/her pronoun default, and the genre-notes toggle that Workspace's own translate path includes — and defaults to `--style-preset audio_drama` even for a narration-type drama. Some of these settings (pronoun default, style preset, genre toggle, locale) are also only ever stored in browser session state, never the database, so the CLI structurally can't read them even if it tried. Re-verify the exact current gap list before fixing — this project's own CLI/UI parity rule (`CLAUDE.md`) already covers the general principle.
4. **Design gap, not a bug: imported novel text never reaches novel narration — plausible, not independently traced end to end.** `sources/pipeline.save_novel_text` writes imported chapters into the same `raw_novel_context.txt` used for Whisper priming (audio dramas) and glossary pairing. For a novel-type drama, nothing in the narration UI appears to load or display that file as narration source text — narration's own text box (`novel_narration_text`) is fed from `ocr_text_<id>`, a different session-state key entirely. Worth a closer look at implementation time to confirm the gap and decide the fix (load the raw-novel file as a narration-text default when present, at minimum), rather than assumed and fixed blind.
5. **`sc_fr_matches` (Scanlate's find-and-replace preview-match store) isn't scoped by drama** — folded into Step 25o's own fix rather than listed as a separate item; noted here only so it isn't lost if 25o is picked up piecemeal.
6. **The hand-off "Retry" button can raise uncaught** — `tabs/sources_tab.py:86-89` calls `front_door.preview` with no `try`/`except` around it, so a `SourceError` or the new `TermsProhibited` (Step 25g) propagates uncaught from that one specific button, unlike the rest of the Sources tab's own error handling. Small, easy fix: wrap it the same way the surrounding code already handles these exceptions.

**Exit:** N/A for most items, per this project's own established convention for bundled bug-tracking steps (Step 9e/9f/25d). Items 1 and 2 are real enough to be worth their own small regression test whenever picked up.

**Built and pushed (`claude/step-25r-roadmap-dwuk8u`), reviewed and approved by the planning session — real, well-built, all four addressed items check out.** Independently verified: fetched fresh, confirmed genuinely current. The diff (6 files, +267/-39) fixes: item 1 (Add bubble now persists immediately via `db.save_bubbles` + rerun, and the section moved outside the `if bubbles:` gate); item 2 (the raw-novel uploader's write is now gated behind an explicit "💾 Save this novel upload" button); item 4 folded in as a real fix, not just flagged (imported-novel text from Sources now loads as narration's own fallback default when no OCR/EPUB text is already present); item 3's CLI parity fix correctly and honestly scoped — folds in the learned style profile and per-line emotion guidance (both DB-backed) while correctly leaving out the pronoun-default/genre-notes toggles (session-state-only, structurally unreachable from the CLI without a schema change), and defaults `--style-preset` to the same per-content-mode default Workspace uses; item 6's Retry button now wraps `front_door.preview` in the same `ChallengeDetected`/`SourceError` handling the rest of the tab uses. ### Step 25s — Fix: Sources' "Import video" can silently overwrite an existing drama's audio with no confirmation
Found by a second dispatched adversarial QC review (2026-09-27, scoped to areas the first pass covered lightly — `dub.py`, `background_jobs.py`, the newer source adapters, `cli.py`, and more), **independently re-verified by direct code read before writing this step** — not taken on the review's word. The most severe finding of that second pass.

**The bug.** `sources/front_door.import_video` (`sources/front_door.py:170-195`) takes a `drama_id` and, when not "audio only," unconditionally does `core.extract_audio_from_video(path, os.path.join(ddir, "audio.wav"))` — writing directly to that drama's `audio.wav` — then `db.update_drama(drama_id, audio_filename="audio.wav", source_video_filename=..., source_url=url, ...)`, repointing the drama's audio to the new file. The "audio only" path is the same shape: `db.update_drama(drama_id, audio_filename=os.path.basename(path), ...)`. Its caller, `tabs/sources_tab.py:113-128`, offers a plain `_drama_picker("Into drama", ...)` that lists **every** drama in the library — including ones already fully transcribed, translated, and dubbed — with no filter for "empty dramas only" and no warning about what importing into an already-populated drama will do. Clicking "⬇️ Import video" overwrites that drama's audio file and repoints it immediately, no confirmation step of any kind.

**Trigger:** pick any existing, already-worked-on drama from Sources' "Into drama" list, paste a video URL, click Import. The drama's audio is silently replaced — every existing line's timing, and any completed dub, now describes audio that no longer matches what's on disk.

1. **Add an explicit, separate confirmation when the picked drama already has audio** (`audio_filename` already set) — same "destructive actions need a separate, explicit confirmation, defaulting to No" pattern this project already uses elsewhere (Step 10's uninstaller, this same QC pass's own Step 25k's zip-validation rework). A drama with no audio yet (a genuinely new import target) needs no extra step; one that already has content does.
2. **Consider narrowing the picker itself** to visually distinguish (or default-filter to) dramas with no existing audio, so accidentally picking a populated one is less likely in the first place — a UI-level mitigation on top of item 1's confirmation, not a replacement for it.
3. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm the exact current shape of `import_video`/`_drama_picker` (line numbers may have shifted) before changing the flow.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms importing a video into a drama that already has `audio_filename` set requires an explicit confirmation step before the existing audio is touched.
- A test confirms importing into a drama with no existing audio still works with no extra friction (the confirmation is conditional, not universal).
- Manual check: pick an already-transcribed drama from Sources' "Into drama" list, attempt to import a different video into it, and confirm the app requires an explicit confirmation before overwriting the existing audio — then confirm declining leaves the drama's audio and lines untouched.

**Built and pushed (`claude/step-25s-roadmap-vjvh63`), reviewed and approved by the planning session — real, well-built, both items 1 and 2 addressed.** Independently verified: fetched fresh, confirmed genuinely current. The diff (2 files, +62/-5) tags any drama with existing audio "⚠️ has audio" in the picker (item 2), and requires an explicit confirmation checkbox before "Import video" is enabled when the picked drama already has audio (item 1) — a drama with no existing audio needs no extra step. Ran the branch's own tests directly: `test_sources_tab.py`, 9 passed, 0 failed. Full combined trial-merge suite (with 25m/25n/25r together): 2490 passed, 46 skipped, 0 failed. Approved.

**Built and merged, PR #102 — opened and merged directly by the planning session.** CI failed once on `test_background_jobs.py::TestNotifyOnCompletion`, a test this step's diff never touches (25s only changes `tabs/sources_tab.py`) — re-ran the failed job via the GitHub API, came back green, confirming a pre-existing timing-sensitive flake (same class already documented in Step 23i's own PR), not a real regression. No re-review needed since this exact content was already verified above.

### Step 25t — Fix: `ui_theme.py`'s tab-bar styling is a dead selector on the installed Streamlit version
Flagged by Step 12's own PR (#89) as a real, out-of-scope finding, confirmed directly, now given its own step.

**The bug.** `ui_theme.py`'s tab-bar styling (`.stTabs [data-baseweb="tab"]`, present in both `inject_css` for the light theme and `inject_dark_css` for the dark theme) targets a selector that Streamlit's rendered DOM no longer produces on the confirmed-installed version, 1.64.0 (Step 12) — tabs now carry `role="tab"`, not a `data-baseweb="tab"` attribute. The custom tab-bar styling, in both light and dark mode, has therefore never actually applied since at least this version; the app has been running on Streamlit's own default tab-bar appearance this whole time without anyone noticing, since nothing errors — the selector just silently matches nothing.

1. **Update the selector to target the DOM Streamlit 1.64 actually renders.** Re-verify the live rendered markup directly (inspect a real running instance's DOM, don't guess from memory or from Streamlit's changelog) before writing the new selector — confirm `role="tab"` is in fact what's present today, and whether any other attribute changed alongside it that the old selector also assumed.
2. **Apply the fix in both `inject_css` and `inject_dark_css`** — this is two copies of essentially the same rule, and both need the same correction or the fix will only half-apply (working in one theme, still broken in the other).
3. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm the exact current shape of both functions (line numbers/surrounding CSS may have shifted since Step 12) before changing the selector.

**Exit:**
- Manual check: open the app in both light and dark theme (Settings' theme toggle) and confirm the tab bar visibly picks up the intended custom styling in both, not Streamlit's stock appearance. No automated test is realistic here — this is a CSS-selector-against-Streamlit's-own-rendered-DOM fix, not app logic, consistent with how this project treats other CSS-only fixes.

**Merged as PR #108** — opened and merged directly by this planning session after independent verification: confirmed the new `.stTabs [role="tablist"]` / `.stTabs [data-testid="stTab"]` selectors are genuinely emitted by the actual installed Streamlit 1.64.0 bundle (grepped the real minified JS at `/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/streamlit/static/static/js/index.CcFifQPt.js` and found the literal `"data-testid":\`stTab\`` and `role:\`tablist\`` strings), not just a plausible guess. Trial-merged cleanly, CI green. Manual check (both themes) still pending — no automated test, per this step's own Exit condition.

### Step 25u — Fix: Navigator and Discover's baihehub search require an API key even when Ollama is selected
Self-flagged in Step 25f's own PR (#90) as a real, out-of-scope finding, confirmed directly by the planning session, now given its own step.

**The bug, two related but distinct manifestations.** `tabs/navigator_tab.py`: `nav_api_key = synced_api_key_input("API key *(required)*", nav_engine_choice, "nav_api_key")` is required unconditionally — `_nav_missing` appends "an API key" and disables the "🧭 Translate page + get navigation steps" button whenever `nav_api_key` is empty, regardless of which engine is selected. Ollama is a local engine that needs no key at all, so selecting it still fully blocks the button until a key is typed in anyway, even though nothing will ever use it. `tabs/discover_tab.py`'s baihehub search is a milder version of the same gap: `bh_api_key` being empty makes `engine = None` in that block, which skips `title_library.translate_query_to_zh` entirely — so with Ollama selected and no key set, the search silently sends the raw, untranslated English query directly against baihehub's Chinese-language database instead of being blocked outright, quietly returning poor or empty results with no explanation.

1. **Both pickers should skip the API-key requirement specifically when the selected engine is Ollama** — matching how every other engine picker in the app already treats a local, no-key-needed engine. Navigator's button should become usable with Ollama selected and no key set; Discover's baihehub search should still route the query through Ollama for translation in that case, not silently fall back to sending it untranslated.
2. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm both call sites' exact current shape (line numbers may have shifted) before changing the gating logic — check whether either has changed since Step 25f in a way that affects this fix.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms Navigator's "🧭 Translate page + get navigation steps" button is enabled (not blocked on a missing API key) when Ollama is the selected engine.
- A test confirms Discover's baihehub search still routes the query through translation when Ollama is selected with no API key set, rather than silently searching the untranslated query.
- Manual check: select Ollama with no API key configured anywhere, confirm Navigator's button is usable and produces real translated labels/steps, and confirm a baihehub search still translates the query to Chinese before searching.

**Merged as PR #109** — opened and merged directly by this planning session after independent verification: read the full diff (`_nav_needs_key`/`_bh_needs_key = engine_choice != "ollama"` gating both the missing-key block and the label text in both files, Discover still builds a real `engine` and still translates the query when Ollama is selected with no key), trial-merged cleanly, ran `tests/test_discover_tab.py` + `tests/test_navigator.py` directly (14/14 passed), CI green. Manual check still pending.

### Step 25v — Fix: two real bugs in the just-merged mangaz.com adapter (Step 23l, PR #106) — the ticket cookie can be lost across a redirect, and a malformed manifest crashes instead of failing cleanly (a third claimed bug, search() returning no results, was a confirmed false positive)
Found by a fresh QC pass on the just-merged Step 23l code, relayed by the user with the instruction to hold off on any action until told what to do. **All three independently re-verified by direct code read** against the real merged `sources/adapters/mangaz.py` and `sources/http.py` before writing this up — none taken on the review's word alone.

**Bug 1 — CORRECTED, this was a false positive, not a real bug.** Originally claimed: `search()` passes the whole `<body>` to `_parse_cards`' non-recursive `<li>` scan, which "real HTML never" puts `<li>` as direct children of. **That reasoning assumed a full HTML page; it isn't one.** `search()`'s endpoint (`/title/addpage_renewal`) is called with `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` — an AJAX partial-refresh endpoint that returns a bare HTML *fragment* (sibling `<li>` elements meant to be spliced into an existing `<ul>` by client-side JS, not a full document with its own wrapping list container). When such a fragment is parsed, its top-level `<li>` siblings do become direct children of whatever root the parser synthesizes (`<body>`) — exactly the shape `_parse_cards`' non-recursive scan was written for. The implementing session caught this by re-running the actual adapter against real HTML captured from the live site while building Step 23l (not a guess): it returns all 50 real results. The existing test fixture (`tests/test_sources_mangaz.py`'s `LATEST_HTML`, predating this step) already encodes the same fragment shape and passes, which should have been checked before this bug was written up. **Lesson**: verify a claimed HTML-structure bug against the endpoint's actual real response shape (or an existing passing test fixture for it) before treating "here's what full-page HTML usually looks like" as confirmation.

**Bug 2 — the ticket cookie can be silently lost across a redirect, producing a false "site changed" error (`sources/http.py:115-120`, consumed by `mangaz.py:285-292`).** `_requests_transport`'s `Response.cookies` is built from `dict(r.cookies)`, where `r` is the *final* response object `requests` returns after following redirects. Confirmed directly against `requests`' own source in this environment: `HTTPAdapter.build_response()` populates each individual response's `.cookies` only from that one hop's own Set-Cookie headers (`extract_cookies_to_jar(response.cookies, req, resp)` on a fresh jar) — cookies set by an *intermediate* redirect hop are folded into the session's own cookiejar (`self.cookies`) but never copied onto the final response's own `.cookies` attribute. If mangaz.com's HEAD `/virgo/view/<id>` ticket request is redirected (a plausible real shape for a session/ticket endpoint) and the `virgo!__ticket` cookie is set on that redirect hop rather than the final response, `_fetch_ticket`'s `resp.cookies.get("virgo!__ticket")` returns `None` even though the site really did issue a valid ticket — raising `LayoutChanged("a virgo!__ticket cookie in the ticket response")`, a misleading "site changed" failure for what's actually a working, unchanged site.

**Bug 3 — a malformed-but-truthy decrypted manifest crashes with a raw traceback instead of a clean adapter error (`sources/adapters/mangaz.py:217-244` combined with its caller at `:414-422`).** `decrypt_page_manifest`'s own validation is `if not manifest.get("Images") or not manifest.get("Location"): raise LayoutChanged(...)` — a truthiness check only, not a type check. If the decrypted JSON has `Location` present but shaped wrong (e.g. a bare string instead of `{base, st}`) or `Images` present as a list of strings instead of a list of `{file}` dicts, both fields pass this check. `get_pages` then calls `manifest["Location"].get("base", "")` and, per image, `image.get("file")` — neither wrapped in a `try`/`except` — so a shape mismatch raises an uncaught `AttributeError` ('str' object has no attribute 'get') straight out of the adapter, instead of the clean `LayoutChanged("...")` every other malformed-response path in this same file already produces.

1. ~~Fix `search()`~~ — not needed, confirmed a false positive (see above).
2. **Fix `_requests_transport`** in `sources/http.py` to correctly surface cookies set on any hop of a redirect, not just the final one — so no cookie set mid-redirect is ever lost. This is a shared transport function, not mangaz-specific.
3. **Fix `decrypt_page_manifest`'s validation to check shape, not just truthiness** — confirm `Images` is a list and each element is a dict before use, confirm `Location` is a dict, raising `LayoutChanged` on any mismatch — and keep `get_pages`' own use of `.get()` only ever running on now-confirmed-dict values.
4. **Re-verify each fix against the real site** at implementation time, same standing rule as every adapter step — a fix built against a guessed HTML/cookie shape is as risky as the original bug.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms `_requests_transport` correctly surfaces a cookie set on an intermediate redirect hop, not just the final response — using a real `requests.cookies.RequestsCookieJar`, not a plain dict standing in for one, so a real conflict/merge behavior is actually exercised.
- A test confirms `decrypt_page_manifest` raises `LayoutChanged` (not an uncaught exception) on a manifest whose `Images`/`Location` are present but wrongly shaped.
- Manual check: pull a real chapter's pages through the fixed ticket/cookie flow and confirm no false "site changed" error; feed a deliberately malformed (but truthy-shaped) mocked manifest through `get_pages` and confirm a clean adapter error, not a raw traceback.

**First submission (branch `fix-23l-review-findings`) reviewed and sent back, not yet approved.** The `decrypt_page_manifest` shape-check fix (item 3) is correct and well-tested. But the `_requests_transport` fix (item 2) — changing `Response.cookies` to `dict(session.cookies)` (the shared thread-local session's own accumulated cookie jar, read via `_thread_session()` in `sources/http.py`) instead of `dict(r.cookies)` — **introduces a new, worse bug than the one it fixes**: `_thread_session()` is one `requests.Session` reused across *every* HTTP call *any* source adapter makes on that thread for the app's entire runtime, not scoped to one request. `dict()` on a `requests.cookies.RequestsCookieJar` flattens by cookie *name* only, with no domain scoping — reproduced directly: two different hosts each setting a cookie named `session` causes `dict(jar)` to raise `CookieConflictError`, an uncaught crash that would propagate out of `_requests_transport` for every single HTTP call across the whole `sources/` package the moment any two hosts' cookies collide by name (a common, generic cookie name colliding across sites is entirely plausible — and mangaz.com's own two hosts, `www.mangaz.com`/`vw.mangaz.com`, share this same session too). Short of a name collision, it still silently pools cookies from every unrelated host/request made on that thread into one flat dict — a correctness regression for every adapter using this transport, not just mangaz.com. The submitted test (`TestResponseCookiesSurviveRedirects`) doesn't catch this because it mocks cookies as plain dicts rather than real `RequestsCookieJar` objects, so the real conflict/merge behavior was never exercised. **Sent back with this exact reproduction and the original recommended fix direction**: merge cookies from each hop in `r.history` (each hop's own individual, real per-response jar — scoped correctly to just this one call, not shared session state) plus the final response's own `.cookies`, rather than reading from the session-wide jar at all.

**Corrected resubmission (branch `step-25v-mangaz-fixes`) reviewed and merged as PR #111.** The corrected `_requests_transport` merges `r.history[i].cookies` (each hop's own per-response jar) + `r.cookies`, oldest first so a later hop can override an earlier same-named cookie — never `session.cookies`. Independently re-verified: re-ran the original `CookieConflictError` reproduction directly against this branch's code and confirmed it no longer crashes; the new tests use real `requests.cookies.RequestsCookieJar` objects (not the plain-dict mocks the first attempt used) and include a regression test proving the *rejected* approach really would crash, not just that the fix works. `decrypt_page_manifest`'s shape-check fix (`Images` a non-empty list of dicts, `Location` a dict) is unchanged and correct. Base was exactly current `baihe-subtitler` tip (no staleness). Ran `tests/test_sources_core.py` + `tests/test_sources_mangaz.py` directly (61 passed), CI green.

### Step 25w — Fix: four real gaps found chasing down the second QC pass's lost findings — an uncached Discover translation call, two real cost-cap bypasses (Google/DeepL engines, "Fix flagged lines in bulk"), and a GPU-guard that has no effect on `cli.py`
The second adversarial QC pass (which produced Step 25s) claimed 20 issues; only the most severe was independently verified at the time, and the background agent sent to re-verify the other 19 was **interrupted mid-task and never produced a report** — confirmed directly by reading its own transcript, which ends on "[Request interrupted by user]" with no conclusion reached. Rather than treat the original 19 as recoverable, a fresh, independent, more targeted pass was dispatched specifically to resolve the one substantive contradiction left in the record (an earlier third pass had specifically re-checked cost-cap/GPU-guard/redaction and found them clean) and to chase the one category nobody had checked yet (an "always-broken/uncached Discover translation call"). **All four findings below independently re-verified by this session via direct code read** against the real current `baihe-subtitler` tip — none taken on the review's word alone.

**Bug 1 — Discover's "Find a title" translates on every single Streamlit rerun, completely ungated, a real and silent cost leak (`tabs/discover_tab.py:82-96`).** Every other LLM-touching action on this tab ("Search baihehub", "Extract entries", "Fetch & add to library") is behind an `st.button(...)`. This one isn't: `if find_query.strip():` runs unconditionally on every script rerun (Streamlit reruns its whole script on any widget interaction anywhere on the page, per `background_jobs.py`'s own docstring on this exact behavior), and inside it, if the "Title to find" box holds non-Chinese text and a Claude key is set, it calls `title_library.translate_query_to_zh(find_query, _eng)`. Confirmed directly: `translate_query_to_zh` (`title_library.py:26-36`) has no `st.cache_data`/`st.cache_resource` and no session-state memoization keyed on the query at all — it's a plain, uncached `call_with_backoff(engine.translate_batch(...))` every time it's reached. Net effect: leaving a non-Chinese title typed into that box burns one real translate call per unrelated interaction anywhere else in the app, for as long as the box stays populated — silent, uncapped real API spend for what looks like a one-shot lookup.

**Bug 2 — the cost-cap system structurally cannot ever apply to the Google Cloud Translation or DeepL engines, in both the UI and (for Google/DeepL specifically) effectively everywhere caps are supposed to hold (`translate_engines.py:955-1001`, `:2185-2205`, `tabs/workspace_tab.py:3001-3009`).** Confirmed directly: `DeepLEngine` and `GoogleEngine` are the only two translate engine classes that never set `self.last_usage` anywhere. `translate_lines_with_engine`'s spend accumulator only runs `if hasattr(engine, "last_usage"):` (line 2185) — false for both, every time — so `spent` stays `0.0` for an entire run no matter how many lines go through, and the cap check at line 2210 (`if cost_cap_usd is not None and spent >= cost_cap_usd ...`) can structurally never fire for these two engines. On top of that, `tabs/workspace_tab.py`'s own `_cap_applies = (engine_choice in ("claude", "deepseek", "gemini") and ...)` (line 3001) explicitly excludes `google`/`deepl` from the cap UI entirely — no monthly-cap refusal check, no cost estimate/warning, no job-cap input, and `_cost_cap` stays `None` at job start (line 3587-3590). Both are real, metered, pay-per-character services (unlike Ollama/NLLB, correctly excluded as genuinely free/local) — a user who sets a monthly spending cap in Settings gets **zero enforcement** translating anything through Google or DeepL.

**Bug 3 — "🔁 Re-transcribe + re-translate flagged lines" bypasses the cost-cap system entirely, a separate gap from Bug 2 (`tabs/workspace_tab.py:1032-1080`, button at `:4483-4495`).** `run_fix_flagged_lines_job` loops over every flagged line and calls `engine.translate_batch([ln.zh], ...)` directly per line — a real translation call, logged to `db.log_usage` for history/accounting, but with **no `cost_cap_usd` parameter, no `resolve_cost_cap` call, no monthly-cap refusal check, and no spend accumulation checked against any cap** anywhere in the function or its call site — confirmed directly, neither exists in this function unlike the main "Translate all lines" path and the CLI, both of which do resolve and enforce a cap. A drama with many flagged lines, fixed repeatedly, has completely unbounded spend regardless of the user's configured monthly cap — the same category of spend the cap system exists to police, reached through a different button.

**Bug 4 — the GPU-guard (Step 5c) has no effect at all on `cli.py`, a real and easily-reachable concurrency gap (`background_jobs.py`'s own module docstring; confirmed `cli.py` never imports `background_jobs` anywhere).** `background_jobs.py`'s guard state (`_jobs`, `_gpu_queue`) is plain module-level Python state, single-process and in-memory by the module's own explicit docstring. `cli.py` — whose own docstring markets it for unattended overnight/background runs across many dramas, i.e. exactly the scenario where someone might also have the Streamlit app open — never imports `background_jobs` and never calls `start_job`/`start_process_job`; every GPU-touching CLI command (`align`'s `transcribe_for_timing`, `diarize`'s `diarize.diarize`, `dub`'s `build_dub_track`/`build_narration_track`, `translate --engine ollama`) runs completely outside the "one GPU job at a time" guard. Since the guard is pure in-process state, a second OS process (the CLI) is invisible to it and vice versa — running an overnight CLI dub batch while separately using the live UI for a GPU-touching job (transcription, diarization) hits exactly the VRAM-contention scenario Step 5c's own guard docstring says it was built to prevent.

1. **Fix Bug 1**: gate Discover's title-translation behind an explicit action (a button, or at minimum a cache keyed on the exact query string so an unchanged box doesn't re-translate every rerun) — matching how every other LLM call on this same tab is already gated.
2. **Fix Bug 2**: give `GoogleEngine`/`DeepLEngine` a real `last_usage` (Google's REST response and DeepL's SDK both expose character/token counts usable for a cost estimate — verify the real response shape before wiring this, don't guess), and remove the `_cap_applies` exclusion once they can actually report usage; until usage reporting is wired up, at minimum surface a clear "cost cap does not apply to this engine" notice in the UI rather than silently omitting the whole cap UI.
3. **Fix Bug 3**: route `run_fix_flagged_lines_job` through the same `resolve_cost_cap`/monthly-refusal/job-cap machinery `translate_lines_with_engine` already uses, rather than calling `engine.translate_batch` directly with no cap check.
4. **Fix Bug 4**: make `cli.py`'s GPU-touching commands participate in the same guard — since `background_jobs`' guard is in-process, this needs a cross-process mechanism (a lock file or the existing SQLite database as the shared coordination point, not a new subsystem) so a CLI run and the live UI can't both hold a GPU-touching job at once. Re-verify the exact current shape of both `background_jobs.py`'s guard and `cli.py`'s command dispatch before changing either.
5. **Re-verify each fix against the real engines/CLI at implementation time** — this step touches billing-relevant code paths for two real paid services (Google, DeepL) and a resource-contention guard; a guessed fix here is worse than no fix.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms Discover's title-translation doesn't fire again on an unrelated rerun when the query text hasn't changed.
- A test confirms a job using the Google or DeepL engine is actually subject to a configured cost cap (or, if usage reporting isn't wired up yet, that the UI clearly says the cap doesn't apply rather than silently hiding the cap controls).
- A test confirms "Fix flagged lines in bulk" stops (or refuses to start) when a configured cost cap would be exceeded, the same way "Translate all lines" already does.
- A test or manual check confirms a CLI GPU-touching command and a live UI GPU-touching job can't both proceed concurrently once the cross-process guard is in place.
- Manual check: set a low monthly cost cap in Settings, run a real translation job through Google and through DeepL, and confirm the cap is actually respected (or the UI honestly says it isn't yet); leave a non-Chinese title in Discover's "Find a title" box, click something else nearby, and confirm no repeat translation call fires; start a CLI dub/transcribe run and, while it's active, try to start a GPU-touching job from the live UI, confirming the second one queues rather than running concurrently.

**Merged as PR #112** — opened and merged directly by this planning session after a two-round independent review. Round 1 confirmed all four fixes correct and well-built (Discover's exact-query-string cache; real per-character usage reporting wired into `GoogleEngine`/`DeepLEngine`; `run_fix_flagged_lines_job` now resolves and enforces the same cap "Translate all lines" does; a genuinely well-designed cross-process `gpu_lock` table in the shared `library.db`, with atomic acquire and heartbeat/staleness handling for a crashed holder, correctly wired into both `background_jobs.py`'s promotion logic and `cli.py`'s GPU-touching commands, scoped precisely — `diarize`/`align` always, `translate` only for `--engine ollama`, `dub` only via the existing `clone_map_uses_local_model` check, not new code) — but caught one real test gap (a DeepL-specific test failed only because the optional `deepl` package wasn't installed in the review environment, not a code bug) and sent it back. Round 2 confirmed the fix (`pytest.importorskip("deepl")`, exactly as asked) and independently re-ran the full suite: **2606 passed, 47 skipped, 0 failed**, including a clean 18/18 on `test_sources_mangaz.py` (confirming the 4 mangaz failures the user separately saw are a real environment-specific issue in their own sandbox unrelated to this branch). This also closes out the entire "chase down the second QC pass's lost 19 findings" line of work.

### Step 25x — Fix: Reader's "Why this?"/Alternatives/Grammar results stay keyed by drama only, showing a stale line's results after switching to a different line
Found by a fourth, broader adversarial pass explicitly scoped to hunt for staleness bugs (does new data populate live, or need a manual refresh?) at the user's direct request, alongside dead-end and general-bug hunting. **Independently re-verified by direct code read** against the real merged `tabs/reader_tab.py` before writing this up.

**The bug (`tabs/reader_tab.py`, "🔬 Line tools" section, ~lines 336-364).** The line picker's three result caches — `lt_explain_{rdrama['id']}`, `lt_alts_{rdrama['id']}`, `lt_gram_{rdrama['id']}` — are keyed only by drama id, not by which line was selected when "Why this?"/"Alternatives"/"Grammar" was clicked. A few lines below this exact same block, `lt_improved_{_pl_key}` (the "Improve this line" feature) is correctly keyed by `f"{rdrama['id']}_{pl.id}"` — with its own comment explicitly recording why: **"Step 25c: generated rewrites/re-transcriptions are kept per line, not per drama -- keyed per drama, a result generated for one line was still showing (and applicable) after picking another line."** That exact fix was applied to `lt_improved_*` but never extended to the three sibling caches (`lt_explain`/`lt_alts`/`lt_gram`) built the same way in the same section — they still carry the pre-Step-25c bug shape. Trigger: on a page with 2+ lines, click "Why this?" for line A, then pick line B in the "Line" selectbox without re-clicking any of the three buttons — the explanation/alternatives/grammar breakdown shown below still displays line A's stale results under line B's now-shown source/translation text, with nothing indicating it's stale or belongs to a different line.

1. **Apply the same `_pl_key` scoping Step 25c already uses for `lt_improved_*`** to all three of `lt_explain_*`/`lt_alts_*`/`lt_gram_*` — the fix is mechanical, not new design: reuse the existing `_pl_key = f"{rdrama['id']}_{pl.id if pl.id is not None else f'idx{pl.idx}'}"` line (currently computed just below this block, for `lt_improved_*` alone) for all four caches, or move its computation earlier in the function so all four can share it.
2. **Re-verify before fixing**: confirm the exact current line numbers/shape of this section (may have shifted) before changing the keys.

**Exit:**
- A test confirms clicking "Why this?"/"Alternatives"/"Grammar" for one line, then switching the line picker to a different line, does NOT show the first line's stale results under the second line's display.
- A test confirms each of the three results is still shown correctly when re-selecting a line that was previously inspected (not just cleared and never shown again).
- Manual check: on a real drama with 2+ lines, click all three buttons for line 1, switch to line 2, and confirm none of the three results sections show line 1's content.

**Merged as PR #113** — opened and merged directly by this planning session after independent verification: base was exactly current `baihe-subtitler` tip, diff read in full (`_pl_key` computation moved earlier and applied to all four caches, exactly the mechanical fix asked for), both new tests pass, full suite clean (2628 passed, 46 skipped, 0 failed).
